# [I3 — Changing sampling frequency and season](../hypodrafts/I3.md "Changing sampling frequency and season")

*Generated by `scripts/pages/hypodraft_i3.py` from the draft as committed at `c601feb`. Counts of files held in this repository are read live. Counts that session made from external sources or from one-off runs are quotations of that commit - what the draft reported, shown as such, not re-derived by the build.*


**Claim (HYPOTHESES.md).** "A deficit indicator built from the worst month is biased by
how often you sampled that month. More visits find more extremes." Outcome [O1](../HYPOTHESES.md "Oxygen deficit").

Neighbour [I1](../hypodrafts/I1.md "Changing station network") asks *which stations*. This asks *how often, and when in the year* — temporal
aliasing of a quantity that varies faster than the sampling interval.

## The hypothesis splits in two, and only one half is scoreable

**I3a — count and window.** An extremal indicator (annual minimum, worst-month value,
days-below-threshold) is a first-order statistic. Its expectation moves with the number of
draws and with which months the draws fall in. Testable in full.

**I3b — diel phase.** Oxygen has a diel cycle; daylight at [55](../SOURCES.md#F-cc50790188)°N runs ~[7](../SOURCES.md#F-42fe5e156a) h (December) to
~[17](../SOURCES.md#F-960ddba5af) h (June), so working-hours sampling walks the diel phase with season. **There is no
time-of-day column anywhere in the archive.** Verified across all four ODA exports:
`ctd.csv.gz` ([34](../SOURCES.md#F-25eafec29d) fields), `lys.csv.gz` ([30](../SOURCES.md#F-d5aaa40e38)), `maaledybde.csv.gz` ([19](../SOURCES.md#F-9604888a28)), `stations.csv` ([17](../SOURCES.md#F-19f732a9f5))
— every temporal field is `YYYYMMDD`. Class 6, absent dimension: not recoverable, not
boundable, not countable. I3b is **unscoreable, not unsupported**, and no result below
speaks to it. Nothing here licenses a claim that the diel confound is absent or small.

## Observable consequence (I3a), stated to be falsified

If I3a is right, an extremal severity indicator computed under **fixed effort and a fixed
calendar window** will show a different temporal pattern than the same indicator computed
on whatever visits each station-year happens to contain. If the two paths coincide inside
the resampling envelope, I3a is refuted as an explanation of the [O1](../HYPOTHESES.md "Oxygen deficit") trend.

Two directions must be separated, because they push opposite ways and the data show they
nearly cancel:

- **Count.** More draws, lower minimum, mechanically.
- **Window.** Sparse programmes are not thin versions of dense ones — they are
  late-summer-targeted. Station-years with ≤[3](../SOURCES.md#F-ee0a9b65d5) near-bed oxygen months put [50.2](../SOURCES.md#F-10d3ed95a3)% of their
  observations in August–September; station-years with ≥[9](../SOURCES.md#F-9fa56245aa) months are near-flat ([7.2](../SOURCES.md#F-7dbea1dca4)%–[8.8](../SOURCES.md#F-1b0ce7ecf5)%
  per month). Sparse sampling therefore *finds* hypoxia while having few chances to.

## Data, with counts I verified

`docs/data/areas/stations_series.{json,bin}` — [679,422](../SOURCES.md#F-b61d7944ec) station-months, [1,415](../SOURCES.md#F-fff0060a3d) stations,
[9](../SOURCES.md#F-81bea72caf) variables, 1980–2026, month index [0](../SOURCES.md#F-206716437b)–[560](../SOURCES.md#F-65edb63100). Variable `oxy_bed`: **[76,980](../SOURCES.md#F-a95c664ddf)** station-months,
**[11,289](../SOURCES.md#F-79f28bcfc0)** station-years.

- Class 1, value error: [432](../SOURCES.md#F-5e87cd6b66) values ≤ [0](../SOURCES.md#F-08f97cade9) and [40](../SOURCES.md#F-8796915a35) > [20](../SOURCES.md#F-b58ed93cd0) mg/l. Dropped; [76,508](../SOURCES.md#F-926a88b96f) retained.
- Class 3, aggregation: the product is a **monthly median**, so within-month replication is
  gone. It is not gone from the archive. The complete visit register
  `data/raw/oda/maaledybde.csv.gz` ([151,203](../SOURCES.md#F-eea1e4eb92) soundings, [1,429](../SOURCES.md#F-6963a584e4) stations, 1980–2026) has
  **[50.9](../SOURCES.md#F-459a26479f)%** of its [83,011](../SOURCES.md#F-1ef4ec152d) station-months carrying ≥[2](../SOURCES.md#F-43e5c5c214) distinct sampling days. Oxygen rows
  specifically, over a [6](../SOURCES.md#F-98363c3293)M-row prefix of `ctd.csv.gz` ([992](../SOURCES.md#F-93cd89e6f0) stations, [31,539](../SOURCES.md#F-44e320704d) station-months —
  a prefix, **not** a population estimate): **[31.9](../SOURCES.md#F-bc86e3157f)%**. So the monthly panel can test count
  and window; it cannot test sub-monthly variance, and the raw file can.
- Class 6: no time of day (above). Class 7 applies to `oxysat_*` (computed from
  oxygen+temperature+salinity) — not used here.

## The null under the constraint I impose

**Constraint:** station-years with all twelve calendar months present — **[2,314](../SOURCES.md#F-7ad1812267)** of [11,289](../SOURCES.md#F-5204a01225).
Effort is fixed at [12](../SOURCES.md#F-32f72da34a) and station composition is fixed inside each unit, so nothing is
compared across differently-observed units.

**The null is computed, not assumed, and the naive one is wrong.** Marginally, minima do
*not* fall with visit count: median annual minimum is [4.73](../SOURCES.md#F-da7ecd8333) mg/l at [3](../SOURCES.md#F-8feea350c8) visits and [6.30](../SOURCES.md#F-ac53dd2962) at [12](../SOURCES.md#F-02f5449a13).
A null of "severity rises with count" would be inverted by the window effect. Within the
[2,314](../SOURCES.md#F-2da044fb7b) fixed units, drawing month-sets from each station-year's own twelve values ([200](../SOURCES.md#F-981577be99) Monte
Carlo draws):

| indicator on the same [2,314](../SOURCES.md#F-e49e1baaad) station-years | mean min (mg/l) | P(min < [4](../SOURCES.md#F-72cda7999d)) |
|---|---|---|
| min over all [12](../SOURCES.md#F-a5637d646e) months | [5.69](../SOURCES.md#F-ea2705887e) | [0.250](../SOURCES.md#F-84d374c9f9) |
| E[min over [3](../SOURCES.md#F-3633996688) months drawn at random] | [7.23](../SOURCES.md#F-7a31f4fd73) | [0.058](../SOURCES.md#F-115e6b96df) |
| min over the fixed window {Jul, Aug, Sep} | [5.93](../SOURCES.md#F-e8f6b87dfc) | [0.219](../SOURCES.md#F-11f378d021) |

Count alone moves exceedance by **[4.3](../SOURCES.md#F-fd538e917e)×**; fixing the window to Jul–Sep recovers almost all
of the [12](../SOURCES.md#F-201b1cd15c)-month signal from [3](../SOURCES.md#F-c5e3501668) draws. That table *is* the null: the per-station-year
resampling distribution of the indicator, against which any observed path is scored.

## Procedure

1. Build the effort-matched panel: station-years containing all of Jul, Aug and Sep —
   **[6,802](../SOURCES.md#F-cae002c94b)** units; **[8,771](../SOURCES.md#F-0ca2e879a1)** have ≥[2](../SOURCES.md#F-0d23ac1184) of the three. [323](../SOURCES.md#F-0c1db5f5a8) stations carry ≥[10](../SOURCES.md#F-9688e8a123) such years,
   [225](../SOURCES.md#F-a0c96d2428) carry ≥[15](../SOURCES.md#F-1cccd89a1b), spanning 1980–2026 ([789](../SOURCES.md#F-52506c4b33) / [2,411](../SOURCES.md#F-5437b7e181) / [2,006](../SOURCES.md#F-78da94a1d7) / [1,697](../SOURCES.md#F-5228033fd5) / [1,091](../SOURCES.md#F-b3d55ac988) by decade band).
2. Compute the severity indicator twice per station-year: (a) on all available months,
   (b) on exactly {Jul, Aug, Sep}. Never aggregate to water bodies; the unit is the station.
3. For each unit, draw [200](../SOURCES.md#F-8b70b124fa) month-sets of the same size from that unit's own values to get
   the null envelope for (a). Score the observed path of (a) against it.
4. Regress each indicator on year with station fixed effects. Compare slopes and the year-
   to-year path of (a) and (b).
5. Repeat with the Aug–Sep window and with a [2](../SOURCES.md#F-e6b64d51c5)-of-[3](../SOURCES.md#F-a9e48a6a8f) window, as sensitivity.

## What a result would and would not license

**Would.** If (b) is flat where (a) trends, or the slopes differ beyond the envelope, then
the [O1](../HYPOTHESES.md "Oxygen deficit") severity trend is partly a trend in sampling design, and every extremal indicator in
this project must be recomputed effort-matched. If (a) and (b) agree, I3a is falsified for
extremal indicators at monthly resolution — a real result, and the stronger one.

**Would not.** It says nothing about (i) I3b, the diel confound, which stays unscoreable;
(ii) sub-monthly variance, which needs the raw daily file, not this panel; (iii) *rate*
indicators, already shown robust to effort and station composition here — this test is
about extremal statistics only, where the count dependence is structural; (iv) which
stations were observed, which is [I1](../hypodrafts/I1.md "Changing station network")'s.
